source_span: A higher expected path for oil prices means disinflation will be slower, and more restrictive policy also weighs on growth in 2027.
source_chain: Persistent oil-price shock (supply disruptions, benign de-escalation scenario abandoned) therefore stickier inflation (core PCE raised to 3.2% 2026 / 2.7% 2027) and softer growth (2027 GDP cut to 2.3% from 2.6%, payrolls to 50k/mo, unemployment 4.3%) therefore two more 25bp hikes (Dec + March) to 4.25-4.50% terminal. Invalidation (from the companion FOMC-reaction note, same author bank): faster Middle East de-escalation or quicker disinflation means the Fed hikes only once more, in December, not twice.
pulse_chain: Morgan Stanley switches its baseline to a sustained oil risk premium (45% probability) therefore raises core PCE to 3.2%/2.7%, cuts 2027 GDP to 2.3%, trims payrolls to 50k/mo with unemployment at 4.3% therefore expects two more 25bp hikes (Dec + March) to 4.25-4.50%. Invalidation: faster Middle East de-escalation or quicker disinflation leaves only one more hike, in December.
why: The pulse reproduces Morgan Stanley's exact oil-shock-to-inflation-to-growth-to-hikes sequence, the correct probability (45%), the correct figures, and the correct invalidation condition, attributed to the correct bank.
